title: The Uncertainty Score: How Confident Are We in Rajasthan Royals Player Rankings?
dek: Every ranking of Rajasthan Royals' batters hides uncertainty. Bootstrap intervals show how confident anyone can really be that one batter is ahead of another.
excerpt: Ranked by strike rate since 2024, most neighbouring pairs of Rajasthan Royals' leading batters have overlapping uncertainty intervals. The order is less certain than any league table makes it look.
author: CricField Editorial Desk
keyTakeaways: Of the {{ev:un-pairs}} adjacent pairs in Rajasthan Royals' top-{{ev:un-n}} strike-rate ranking since 2024, {{ev:un-ov}} have overlapping ninety-five per cent intervals.
{{ev:un-wide}} has the widest interval, {{ev:un-wide-w}} strike-rate points across.
Overlapping intervals mean the order between those batters is not settled by the data.

sections.heading: Rankings Without Error Bars
body: Player rankings are usually shown as a clean list. But every strike rate comes from a limited number of innings, and a few innings more or less could change the order.
CricField resampled each of Rajasthan Royals' eight busiest batters' innings since 2024 two thousand times to estimate how much each strike rate could plausibly vary.

sections.heading: How Settled Is the Order?
body: Of the {{ev:un-pairs}} adjacent pairs in the ranking, {{ev:un-ov}} have overlapping ninety-five per cent intervals, so the data does not clearly separate them.
{{ev:un-wide}} has the widest interval, {{ev:un-wide-w}} strike-rate points across. The table lists every batter's interval.

sections.heading: An Uncertainty Score
body: A simple uncertainty score for any ranking is the share of adjacent pairs whose intervals overlap. For Rajasthan Royals' batting order of merit, it is {{ev:un-ov}} of {{ev:un-pairs}}.

sections.heading: Method Notes
body: The bootstrap resamples innings, not balls, so it respects the fact that runs come in bursts. It does not account for changes in role or opposition.
Intervals would narrow with more seasons of data, at the cost of mixing different versions of each player.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Show the Error Bars
body: Rajasthan Royals should read any ranking of their batters alongside its intervals, and treat overlapping players as level.
Decisions that depend on separating them need more evidence than one strike rate.

methodology: Built from the CricField warehouse (Cricsheet ball-by-ball data, regulation innings). Models are fitted on the warehouse itself and described in full here. Generated by scripts/editorial/engine. 95% intervals from 2,000 bootstrap resamples of each batter's innings (seeded).
